svg.title: One UUIDv7, six representations
svg.desc: The UUIDv7 0198abcd-1234-7abc-9def-0123456789ab as UUID text, 16 bytes, plain base64url AZirzRI0eryd7wEjRWeJqw, plain base32hex 06canj8i6htbp7ff04hkaps9lc, masked base64url ap225Qa_y6wN5LQCJgwH0z and masked base32hex daerdp86nv5qo3f4mg12c307qco, with what each form is for, how it sorts and whether case matters. Flipping the last UUID bit changes 22 of 22 masked base64url characters (hAHeRPmJFqjOuXUQnhljgb).
svg.text: Store one UUID. Every form below converts back to it losslessly (masked ones with your key). No mapping table.
36 characters as text · 16 bytes in binary
For UUID columns and UUID-only APIs.
Generate or decode straight into your buffer; errors leave it unchanged.
PLAIN SLUGS · any UUID · no key · the same 128 bits in fewer characters
For short URLs, logs and JSON.
14 characters shorter than UUID text; standard base64url tools decode it.
For case-insensitive filenames and text keys.
Time-range queries on the ID itself; 4 characters longer than base64url.
MASKED SLUGS · UUIDv7 only · need the matching key
Examples use the public demo key
A keyed scramble hides the time and every UUID field, and decodes back to the exact UUID. 132 bits = 42-bit time
offset (~139 years from a start you set) + 74 payload bits + 16-bit check.
Plain and masked base64url can look identical. Choose the reader for the format you issued.
For public IDs that hide the UUID's time and fields.
Your database keeps UUIDs. Only the matching key and settings decode it; keep
For masked IDs in case-insensitive filenames.
5 characters longer. The same UUID, key and settings always give the same slug;
one codec reads both masked alphabets.
Last UUID byte · flip one bit
¹ UUIDv7: sorts by creation millisecond if all IDs share one case and alphabet; not event order within a millisecond.
² Nearby times share prefixes, but ASCII order can swap adjacent milliseconds.
Compare decoded UUIDs, not spellings: one UUID has many valid spellings. A wrong key passes the 16-bit check about once in 65,536
tries and returns another UUID. Masking is not strong encryption.
